ajay: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC review — leaning toward a hybrid approach: Triton for the multi-head attention kernel path, CUTLASS for large matmul/dense paths. Need concrete action items and interface boundaries.

maya: Agree on hybrid. Main worry is fragmented CI and long benchmark runs. Suggest we define a concise perf matrix (seq len x batch x precision) to make decisions reproducible.

chris: We should codify a minimal kernel-adapter interface so both runtimes can plug in without runtime-level hacks. Proposal:
```
class KernelAdapter:
    def init(self, params): pass
    def forward(self, qkv, kv_cache, seq_len, params) -> (output, KernelStatus): pass
    def profile(self, shapes) -> PerfRecord: pass
```
Keep error contract simple (OK, FALLBACK, OOM, UNIMPLEMENTED).

helen: Also need a deterministic fallback policy: if Triton exceeds latency SLO or returns FALLBACK/OOM, runtime should switch to CUTLASS variant and emit a metric + trace. Backoff + canary logic for flapping.

ajay: Agreed. We also need rollout controls in the console: per-model-version kernel selection flags, canary 1%->10%->100%, and automated rollback if perf/regression delta > threshold. Tie these signals into Redwood Optimize.

chris: I'll prototype the adapter shim + a micro-benchmark harness. Will include seq={128,512,2048}, batch={1,8}, prec={fp16,int8-qat} and capture p50/p95/p99. ETA: Wed EOD for initial PR.

maya: I'll own CI integration: nightly perf job that runs the harness and uploads NVTX traces + perf JSON to S3. Need a perf bucket and IAM. @infra-bot can you provision perf bucket `perf-kernel-bench-v2` and add `eng-runtime-perf` group write access?

infra-bot: Provisioning request received. Created bucket `perf-kernel-bench-v2`. IAM: group `eng-runtime-perf` has write. Link: s3://perf-kernel-bench-v2 (please use lifecycle policy to keep storage cheap).

helen: One more: kernel error/status codes must be standardized (KernelStatus enum) so the runtime fallback is deterministic. I'll draft the schema and include retry/backoff semantics.

ajay: Action item summary: 
- chris: kernel adapter shim + microbench PR by Wed EOD (include example traces and p50/p95).
- maya: CI perf job + NVTX trace upload to s3 + nightly schedule.
- helen: KernelStatus enum + fallback SLA table + doc for backoff semantics.
- ajay: rollout plan + console flags + Optimize signal integration.
Let's sync for 30m tomorrow to unblock blockers.

chris: :thumbsup: I'll include a small script to replay traces locally and a simple autotune table for shared-memory settings.

maya: :eyes: Adding to calendar. Can we ensure we capture memory-fragmentation (CUDA mem fragmentation) and RSS? We saw a spike last week on long sequences.

ajay: Yes capture CUDA-allocated, RSS, fragmentation, and tag every run with model_hash and quantization profile. Also include GPU occupancy and shared-memory usage from NVTX.

chris: Quick implementation note: some Triton kernels require extra shared-memory tuning per head-size; the adapter should expose a `tune(params)` hook so we can autotune on first warmup. Fallback thresholds should be parameterized by occupancy.

helen: I'll draft the fallback SLA table (latency multiplier thresholds, retry/backoff, metric names) and add to the RFC follow-up doc.

ajay: Great — thanks everyone. If no blockers after the sync, we'll run the first canary next week.

maya: small request — add `quantization` tag to the perf metadata so Optimize can correlate quality regressions.

ajay: noted.

chris: one last note: include versioned kernel artifact names (kernel_name@git_sha or @build_id) so we can roll forward/back easily.

helen: will add that to the schema.

ajay: meeting scheduled: 30m tomorrow 10:30am PT.

infra-bot: Perf job template: `runs/kernel-perf-nightly --seq 128,512,2048 --batch 1,8 --precision fp16,int8 --upload s3://perf-kernel-bench-v2/$RUN_ID`

chris: thanks — I'll reference that in my PR.

maya: closing loop: I'll create the infra ticket and assign to `eng-infra` for any follow-up networking/IAM items. 

ajay: Thanks — thread closed unless someone needs to add more.
